sn13.11:1.2: Sineru. also known as Neru ([ja379:3.1]()), Meru ([dn32:7.2]()), or Sumeru ([thi-ap17:53.2]()), is the axis mundi, the mountain around which the world revolves in Indian cosmology. The oldest reference is perhaps Taittiriya Āraṇyaka 1.7.1.3, which details its cosmological role. Kaśyapa, the eighth above the seven Sūryas, dwells there constantly, never leaving, while the other Suns illuminate different regions.
